quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone who has been drinking ride a motorcycle. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What is one benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks will take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can help you avoid parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: If you maintain your motorcycle properly and do regular checks, it will continue to run like new.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How often should you completely check your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane beside you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane beside you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the lane beside you as possible. The most important thing is to see the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle needs longer to stop. This includes slippery roads, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright paint is not required.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be driving slowly while looking for a spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver might pull out of a parking space without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired below the legal blood alcohol limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: Which of these clothing items will NOT reduce crash injuries?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Which action lowers the risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers your intentions with signals.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in a position that is hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers your intentions with signals.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat so:

options.text: You can jump off if needed.
Your legs can absorb the shock.
Other drivers can see you better.
You can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs and joints absorb impact force. This keeps the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of these EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Check air pressure, general wear, and tread before riding.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left part of your lane because it:

options.text: Makes it hard to see the vehicle ahead.
Lets the other driver speed up.

questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: What is the helmet law for motorcyclists?

options.text: Required only if carrying a passenger.
Not required if over 21 and licensed for one year or more.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not required if over 21 and licensed for one year or more.
questions.explanation: You do not need a helmet if you are over 21 and have held your motorcycle license for at least one year. However, helmets are recommended for all riders every time.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol or make you sober, though they may keep you awake.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that survived a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle can be much more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does your body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. The time it takes varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you're planning to increase your speed.
Only when there is a lot of traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.
Only if it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one else is around to see it.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses are not enough. Vermont does not require eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding in a vehicle's blind spot?

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to get out of it.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Decide if you can still ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still ride safely.
Don't worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking. Any amount of alcohol can affect your abilities.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. A DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing are best.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Look at the rims and spokes for bends, loose parts, or damage. Check the tire condition and tread. Check all the lights.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.
